DIAGNOSIS READY: Huntington's Disease.

The combination of choreiform movements, progressive dementia (forgetfulness), psychiatric symptoms (irritability, hallucinations), and a strong family history of suicide at age 50 is classic for this autosomal dominant condition. The recent onset of dysphagia likely indicates disease progression. I will not ask further questions; the clinical picture and family history are sufficient for a presumptive diagnosis which can be confirmed with genetic testing if required.
